answer: The strongest sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: an agent gains rights only after verifiable tasks signed by independent counterparties, like miners proving basalt-hard effort before reaching the wharf of commerce. Registration is cheap, but payouts scale with a reputation stake that takes real time to accrue, so each fake agent costs an attacker days of work plus collateral locked against slashing. Mass registration then costs more than any payout, while an honest agent, like a saffron thread, is rare and expensive to fake.
